subject: Post-call recap: GlobalMed \u2014 Private/VPC + air-gap requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <e.chen@globalmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: GlobalMed — Private/VPC + air-gap requirements

Hi Emily — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap of what we covered and proposed next steps so we’re aligned. Please flag anything I missed.

What we heard (pain / drivers):
- Regulatory + data residency: patient records and PHI must remain in an air-gapped environment for certain workloads (California + EU subsets).
- Network constraints: GlobalMed runs through a centrally-managed egress/proxy layer; any Private deployment needs clear IP allowlists, port requirements, and a minimal set of outbound endpoints.
- Auditability: long-term audit logs + integration with your SIEM (Splunk) are required; SOC 2 artifacts and encryption-at-rest/key-management are must-haves.
- Latency expectations: internal workloads require sub-200ms 95th percentile for interactive charting features; bulk batch jobs can be queued.

Proposed solution summary:
- Redwood Private (VPC) deployed into GlobalMed-managed VPC with customer-managed NAT/egress and optional air-gap mode for PHI-only clusters.
- We can provide a compact egress allowlist (IPs & FQDNs) and an offline install variant for the fully air-gapped environment.
- Integrations: KMS/HSM options for key management, and a Splunk-forwarder hook for streaming audit logs.

Attachments I shared: Redwood_SOC2-checklist.pdf (high-level artifacts), network-topology-sketch.png (sketch of where Redwood would sit).

Next steps (owners + tentative timing):
1) GlobalMed IT to confirm networking constraints and whether a partially-air-gapped approach is allowed (Emily, Jacob) —by 2026-03-22.
2) Redwood to produce a 1-page allowlist + port matrix and a short installation runbook for air-gapped install (Marissa/Dev) — by 2026-03-24.
3) Follow-up technical call with GlobalMed infra and security to walk the runbook & clarify SIEM integration (Dev + Rishi + GlobalMed Sec) — propose 60-min slot week of 2026-03-29.

If that looks right, I’ll send the allowlist + runbook draft and lock a time for the technical call.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0138

From: Jacob Alvarez <jacob.alvarez@globalmed.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Chen <e.chen@globalmed.com>, GlobalMed Security <security@globalmed.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GlobalMed — Private/VPC + air-gap requirements

Marissa — thanks for the clear notes. A couple clarifications from the infra/security side: 

1) Air-gap scope: We have two environments — "PHI-Restricted" (completely air-gapped, no outbound internet) and "PHI-Adjacent" (VPC with tightly controlled egress). We will likely ask for both: an on-prem/air-gap for sensitive model training/serving and a VPC-hosted variant for non-PHI workloads.

2) Egress policy: For the VPC option we can allow outbound to a <small set of IPs> but everything must go through our proxy (we'll need SNI passthrough details). If the solution requires outbound DNS resolution, it must be done via our internal resolver (we do not allow direct 8.8.8.8 style lookups).

3) Ports & protocols: Anything that requires persistent outbound connections (e.g., heartbeat or telemetery) must be configurable to work over HTTPS (443) and support proxy headers.

4) Compliance artifacts: send SOC 2 certificate and a short description of how you handle key rotation and KMS integration. We will intake that into our procurement/security questionnaire.

Happy to take the technical call — Jacob (infra) and Laila from security will join. Please add any specifics you can in the allowlist/runbook.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jacob Alvarez <jacob.alvarez@globalmed.com>, Emily Chen <e.chen@globalmed.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GlobalMed — Private/VPC + air-gap requirements

Thanks Jacob — very helpful. Quick answers inline and actions below.

- Air-gap approach: we can support both deployment modes. Our air-gap installer is an offline bundle that your infra team can run behind the firewall; it does not require outbound internet for model serving. For PHI-Adjacent VPC, we’ll provide a minimal outbound footprint.

- Egress/DNS: we’ll provide a runbook that supports SNI passthrough and can be configured to use your internal resolver; DNS lookups by the runtime are only for optional telemetry & model catalog updates — we can completely disable automatic remote catalog checks if you prefer.

- Ports/protocols: runtime telemetry/heartbeats can be configured to use HTTPS (443) via your proxy; we also support a mode with no external telemetry and only local logging shipped to Splunk.

- Compliance artifacts: attaching the SOC2 checklist and a short KMS integration summary. Key rotation is supported via customer KMS APIs; we can document the exact API calls for your KMS vendor (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, or HSM).

Action items we’ll deliver this week:
- Draft allowlist + port matrix (Marissa, by 2026-03-24)
- Air-gap install runbook (Dev, by 2026-03-24)
- Short SPI (Splunk) forwarding notes and sample config (Dev, by 2026-03-24)

Proposed slot for the technical deep-dive: Tue 2026-03-30 10:00 PT (60 min). If that works I’ll send a calendar invite with an agenda.

Marissa

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2-checklist.pdf, network-topology-sketch.png

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: GlobalMed — Private/VPC + air-gap requirements

Appreciate the clarifications, Jacob. I’ll start the air-gap runbook and the minimal allowlist draft today — will send an initial version by end of day Monday (2026-03-22) so you can review before Marissa/Rishi finalize.

A couple notes for the tech call agenda:
- Show the air-gap installer flow and what artifacts we need from GlobalMed (admin credentials for installer runbook, expected firewall change windows).
- Walk the KMS integration options and sample API call (AWS KMS + Azure + HSM).
- Confirm Splunk-forwarder configuration and expected index names / retention.

If anyone from GlobalMed wants to share a high-level network diagram (even a hand-drawn scan), I’ll annotate it quickly to show where the Redwood nodes would land.

Thanks — Dev
